exposure: Mother-child dyads who underwent vaginal delivery
outcome: Autism spectrum disorder diagnosis in offspring
cohort: Two cohorts of mother-child dyads: one with public insurance (910,696 deliveries) and one with private insurance (696,883 deliveries)
finding: The combined evidence from this study and other observational studies does not support a strong association between neuraxial labor analgesia and an increased risk of autism spectrum disorder in offspring, although a small increase cannot be ruled out.
mod_finding: This study found that neuraxial labor analgesia use was not associated with an increased risk of autism spectrum disorder in offspring, even when considering different modes of delivery (vaginal, cesarean, and assisted vaginal).
